subject: Decision: choosing network access pattern for Redwood Private (VPC / PrivateLink / S2S VPN)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jeff Hansen <jeff.hansen@medicorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Options for connecting MediCorp to Redwood Private - quick decision request

Hi Jeff / team,

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion I've sketched three viable network access patterns for Redwood Private: VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (endpoint services), and Site-to-Site VPN. Attached are a one-page diagram and a short cost/ops matrix (redwood-private-access-options-diagram.pdf, cost-comparison-matrix.xlsx).

Quick summary (short bullets):
- VPC peering: lowest latency, but no transitive routing and requires non-overlapping CIDRs; cross-account peering possible but increases management if you have many accounts.
- PrivateLink: strongest isolation (customers only see an ENI), avoids public IPs, simplifies routing and security posture, slightly higher per-GB charges and has single-AZ endpoint considerations unless using NLB in front.
- Site-to-site VPN: fastest to onboard for on-prem, supports overlapping address spaces via NAT, but higher latency, less predictable throughput, and ongoing VPN appliance management.

Our recommendation for a first pilot is to evaluate PrivateLink for the east region (us-east-1) for your non-bursting workloads and reserve a VPN fallback for any on-prem appliances that cannot front a PrivateLink endpoint. If you expect bursty, low-latency steady traffic (tens of Gbps), we'd discuss Dedicated capacity + VPC peering or Direct Connect.

Decision requested: which pattern would you like to pilot (PrivateLink / VPC Peering / S2S VPN)? If PrivateLink, we can provision the endpoint service and share the acceptance steps.

Action items:
- Jeff: confirm pilot choice by 2027-05-14
- Alex/Karthik: prepare step-by-step acceptance & security docs once choice is made
- Marissa: prepare cost estimate for 3-month pilot and 12-month run rate

Thanks,

Alex Martinez
Product Manager, Redwood Private
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-private-access-options-diagram.pdf (diagram), cost-comparison-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jeff Hansen <jeff.hansen@medicorp.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Options for connecting MediCorp to Redwood Private - quick decision request

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from our security/network team:

- Latency: our inference calls are latency-sensitive (p90 target ~50ms from our app region). Can you share measured p99/p90 metrics for each pattern or point to benchmarks?
- Compliance: we need proof that logs can be retained for 12 months and that traffic never traverses the public internet (we prefer PrivateLink or Direct Connect).
- CIDR: we have legacy overlapping ranges in a handful of on-prem sites — PrivateLink sounds better, but can PrivateLink handle multi-account acceptance flows smoothly?

We lean toward PrivateLink for the pilot, but want to validate the latency and the acceptance/automation steps. Also include cost impact for 200k tokens/day approximate traffic.

Jeff
Networking Lead, MediCorp

Subject: Re: Options for connecting MediCorp to Redwood Private - quick decision request

Thanks Jeff — quick tech notes to clarify tradeoffs and answer your questions. I'm pasting the shorttable from our infra notes below and adding a few caveats.

- Latency:
  - VPC peering (same AZ/region): p50 ~5-8ms, p90 ~10-15ms for token-level RPCs inside the region.
  - PrivateLink (NLB fronted endpoint): p50 ~8-12ms, p90 ~18-30ms depending on endpoint scaling and cross-AZ hops. For p90 ~50ms targets at the application layer, PrivateLink is usually fine; p99 can spike if endpoints are pinned to a single AZ.
  - Site-to-site VPN: p50 ~20-40ms and p90 ~50-120ms (depends on WAN MPLS / Internet path), throughput limited by appliance.

- PrivateLink acceptance: our endpoint service supports multi-account acceptance via the AWS console/API. We provide a CloudFormation snippet to automate the acceptance flow; we also provide an IAM role you can use to automate provisioning if you want SREs to run it from your account. PrivateLink requires you to create an interface endpoint in each VPC; acceptance is one-time per account per region for the service.

- Security/compliance: logs can be exported from our control plane and the VPC flow logs can be sent to your S3/CloudWatch with lifecycle policies for 12+ months. We'll include a sample retention policy.

Caveat: If you have overlapping CIDRs and need to talk to multiple AWS accounts simultaneously using peering, peering won't work without renumbering; PrivateLink or VPN + NAT are your options.

Recommendation (technical): Pilot PrivateLink in us-east-1, ensure we run the endpoint across at least two AZs (NLB in front) to stabilize p99, and monitor token-level latency for a week. If you see sustained low-latency high-throughput traffic, transition to Dedicated + VPC peering or consider Direct Connect for predictable bandwidth.

I'll attach the CloudFormation snippet and a minimal runbook after Alex confirms pilot.

— Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: cf-privatelink-accept.yaml (snippet)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Options for connecting MediCorp to Redwood Private - quick decision request

Thanks everyone — quick update and next steps.

Decision: MediCorp confirmed via Jeff that they want to pilot PrivateLink in us-east-1. Jeff noted they will accept the CloudFormation/automation flow and will create the interface endpoint from their account.

Planned runbook (summary):
1) Karthik: provision endpoint service + NLB across 2 AZs and publish entitlement (private link service) — target ready date 2027-05-20.
2) Alex/Marissa: share pilot run-rate estimate and acceptance steps (cost spreadsheet attached).
3) MediCorp (Jeff): create interface endpoint and share acceptance request; perform an initial smoke test with a small token budget.
4) Monitor: run 7-day latency and error SLOs (token-level traces). If p90 < 40ms and error rate < 0.5% we graduate pilot and discuss Dedicated peering for high-throughput patterns.

Open items:
- Marissa to confirm 3-month cost delta for PrivateLink vs VPC peering + Direct Connect.
- Jeff to confirm any compliance evidence required beyond our SOC2 + flow logs (we can export additional audit logs if needed).

I'll upload the runbook and the CloudFormation snippet to the shared Drive once Karthik posts the final CFN.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Alex Martinez
Product Manager, Redwood Private
Redwood Inference
